rules.description: Every reimbursement claim must include all three mandatory documents: Claim Form, Hospital Bill with receipt, and Hospital Discharge Summary.

source.quote: Section 1.1 (Mandatory Claim Documents): Every reimbursement claim submitted under this policy must include all three of the following documents: (1) a completed and signed Claim Form, (2) an itemized original Hospital Bill with receipt, and (3) the official Hospital Discharge Summary. If any of these three required documents is missing, the claim shall be considered incomplete and cannot be processed for reimbursement.

rules.description: 30-day initial waiting period from policy inception date for illness treatments; accidental injury hospitalization is exempt.
exceptions: Hospitalization necessitated solely by an accidental injury sustained after the policy inception date.

source.quote: Section 2.1 (Initial Waiting Period): A mandatory waiting period of 30 days shall apply from the policy inception date. Any hospitalization or medical expenses incurred for treatment of illness during the first 30 days of coverage are strictly excluded from reimbursement, except where hospitalization is necessitated solely by an accidental injury sustained after the policy inception date.

rules.description: Maximum eligible room and boarding coverage is INR 5000 per day; excess room rent is non-payable, and if room rent exceeds INR 5000/day, professional fees and OT charges are payable only in the ratio 5000 / actual daily rate.

source.quote: Section 2.2 (Room Rent Daily Limit and Proportional Deduction): The maximum eligible room and boarding expense covered by the insurer is INR 5000 per day of hospitalization. Any room rent charges incurred in excess of INR 5000 per day are non-payable by the insurer and shall be borne entirely by the insured person. If the actual daily room rent exceeds INR 5000, then professional fees and operation theatre charges are payable only in the ratio 5000 / actual daily rate, with the remaining balance of such charges being non-payable.

rules.description: Cataract surgery reimbursement is subject to a monetary sub-limit of INR 40000 per eye, inclusive of surgeon fees, OT charges, and IOL costs.

source.quote: Section 3.1 (Sub-Limit on Cataract Surgery): Reimbursement for cataract surgery shall be subject to a strict monetary sub-limit of INR 40000 per eye, inclusive of surgeon fees, operating room charges, and intraocular lens costs. Any expenses incurred for cataract surgery in excess of INR 40000 per eye are non-payable by the insurer.

rules.description: Exclusion of specified non-medical administrative and disposable consumable expenses.

source.quote: Section 3.2 (Non-Payable Items Schedule): The following non-medical and administrative items are non-payable and strictly excluded from reimbursement: registration fees, admission processing charges, gloves, face masks, sanitizers, thermometer charges, and luxury patient amenity kits.

rules.description: Medical expenses for the same illness or injury in the 30 days before admission are payable; earlier expenses are non-payable.

source.quote: Section 5.1 (Pre-Hospitalisation Expenses): Medical expenses incurred during the 30 days immediately before the date of admission, for the same illness or injury for which the hospitalisation claim is admissible, are payable. Pre-hospitalisation expenses incurred more than 30 days before the date of admission are non-payable.

rules.description: Medical expenses for the same illness or injury in the 60 days after discharge are payable; later expenses are non-payable.

source.quote: Section 5.2 (Post-Hospitalisation Expenses): Medical expenses incurred during the 60 days immediately after the date of discharge, for the same illness or injury for which the hospitalisation claim is admissible, are payable. Post-hospitalisation expenses incurred more than 60 days after the date of discharge are non-payable.

rules.description: Road ambulance charges are payable up to INR 2000 per hospitalisation.

source.quote: Section 5.3 (Ambulance Charges): Road ambulance charges for transfer to the hospital are payable up to a maximum of INR 2000 per hospitalisation. Any ambulance charges in excess of INR 2000 per hospitalisation are non-payable.

rules.description: Total payable for all claims in a policy year cannot exceed the Sum Insured of INR 500000.

source.quote: Section 5.4 (Sum Insured): The total amount payable for all claims in a policy year shall not exceed the Sum Insured of INR 500000. Any amount claimed in excess of the Sum Insured is non-payable.

rules.description: Cashless treatment needs a Pre-Authorisation Form and the doctor's Cost Estimate, sent 72 hours before a planned admission or within 24 hours of an emergency admission.

source.quote: Section 5.5 (Cashless Pre-Authorisation): Cashless treatment at a network hospital requires a pre-authorisation request containing both of the following documents: (1) a completed Pre-Authorisation Form and (2) the treating doctor's Cost Estimate. For planned hospitalisation the request must reach the insurer at least 72 hours before admission. For emergency hospitalisation the request must reach the insurer within 24 hours of admission.

rules.description: Every existing medical condition must be declared; undeclared conditions found in medical records are referred for medical review.

source.quote: Section 5.6 (Disclosure of Existing Conditions): The insured person must declare every existing medical condition in the claim form or pre-authorisation form. Any medical condition found in the medical records that was not declared shall be referred for medical review before the claim is settled.

ambiguities.description: Pre-existing conditions exclusion references 'as defined under applicable regulations' without defining the applicable regulatory framework, lookback period, or statutory duration within the policy.
ambiguities.issue: Undefined regulatory reference for pre-existing conditions

source.quote: Section 4.1 (Pre-Existing Conditions Exclusion): Any medical condition, ailment, or injury that constitutes a Pre-Existing Condition, as defined under applicable regulations, shall be excluded from coverage until the expiration of the statutory waiting period. Claims arising from or attributable to Pre-Existing Conditions shall not be indemnified.
